doc.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Touring South America and Mexico with Ellington
summary: Ellington wrote the Mexican suite while traveling by DC-3 and playing poorly amplified concerts; flying meant customs and exhausting schedules.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well then of course he did the Latin, the — what was to have been the “Mexican Anticipation” when we went round South America with him, and when we came back then we went to Mexico and he promised to do a Mexican suite. And he was writing that as we traveled round Mexico. He would play a concert — I remember we played a concert in Mexico City and the next morning we left very early in the morning on a DC- 3, you know, remember those old planes? Twin engine? Dakotas. And we’d fly out in that, and then we’d play an outdoor thing in a big arena, the plane was an hour late so part of the audience had gone, and the amplification was awful. They can’t mic, sort of, the bass, and the trombones were amplified enormously and the saxophones — you could hardly hear. But the crowd thought it was splendid you know. Well then we finished that and go back to the hotel, and he’s going to continue writing the “Mexican Anticipation” suite. That’s how he did it — writing all the time that he’s traveling, no matter what the hours. Then he found there was no room service in the hotels, so he said well we’d better go to bed. And then we’d leave the next morning. We’d get up about six o’clock. And do one of those tours was amazing. Makes you wonder how they stood that you know.
For so many years, yeah. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Yeah. And I mean flying simply meant that instead of doing a one-nighter and a bus from city to city, you flew from one city in one country to a city in another country. And you’d have to go through customs, and funny money and all that stuff.
So it wasn’t that much better with the advent of the airplane.
Well it did sort of open up the world, I mean, bigger markets surely.
